newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus cembroides seed cones as symmetric and 1–3.5 cm long, ovoid before opening and broadly depressed-ovoid to nearly globose when open; the thickened apophyses are transversely keeled.
requiredSourceText: broadly depressed-ovoid to nearly globose when open
newRecords.caveat: These are account-level taxonomic descriptors, not population means.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus echinata seed cones as 4–6 cm long, occasionally to 7 cm, lanceoloid or narrowly ovoid before opening and ovoid-conic when open; the central umbo bears an elongate or short, stout, sharp prickle.
requiredSourceText: lanceoloid or narrowly ovoid before opening
elongate to short, stout, sharp prickle
newRecords.caveat: The range is retained as an account-level description, not a population frequency estimate.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus glabra seed cones as 3.5–7 cm long, nearly symmetric, lance-ovoid before opening and ovoid-cylindric when open; the apophyses are only slightly thickened and raised.
newRecords.caveat: The account compares some cone-scale features with P. echinata; this claim reports only the directly stated P. glabra description.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus monticola seed cones as symmetric and 10–25 cm long, lance-cylindric to ellipsoid-cylindric before opening and broadly lanceoloid to ellipsoid-cylindric when open.
requiredSourceText: symmetric, lance-cylindric to ellipsoid-cylindric before opening
broadly lanceoloid to ellipsoid-cylindric when open
newRecords.caveat: The measurement is an account-level range, not a population estimate.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus muricata seed cones as mostly asymmetric, 4–9 cm long, lanceoloid-ovoid before opening and curved-ovoid when open; the apophyses are much thickened and the central umbo forms a stout-based curved claw.
newRecords.caveat: The account separately reports serotiny and persistence; neither behavior is converted here to a general ecology claim.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus ponderosa seed cones as 5–15 cm long, symmetric to slightly asymmetric, conic-ovoid before opening and broadly ovoid when open; the apophyses are thickened, variably raised and transversely keeled.
requiredSourceText: thickened and variously raised and transversely keeled
newRecords.caveat: Cone sizes and shapes are account-level descriptors, not population means.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus pungens seed cones as asymmetric and 4–10 cm long, ovoid before opening and broadly ovoid when open; the apophyses are thickened and strongly keeled, and the central umbo forms a stout curved claw.
newRecords.caveat: The account separately describes variable serotiny; this claim is limited to cone structure and form.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus quadrifolia seed cones as 4–8 cm long, occasionally to 10 cm, ovoid before opening and broadly ovoid to depressed-globose when open; their apophyses are thickened, raised and transversely keeled.
requiredSourceText: broadly ovoid to depressed-globose when open
newRecords.caveat: The source range preserves its occasional 10 cm upper value; it is not a population frequency estimate.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus resinosa seed cones as symmetric and 3.5–6 cm long, ovoid before opening and broadly ovoid to nearly globose when open; the apophyses are slightly thickened, slightly raised and transversely low-keeled.
requiredSourceText: broadly ovoid to nearly globose when open
slightly thickened, slightly raised, transversely low-keeled
newRecords.caveat: This claim records morphology in the cited account; it does not infer a distribution of traits among sampled populations.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus rigida seed cones as symmetric, 3–9 cm long, conic to ovoid before opening and broadly ovoid when open; the firm scales have a distal dark red-brown border, and the apophyses have strong transverse keels.
requiredSourceText: often clustered, symmetric, conic to ovoid before opening
broadly ovoid with flat or slightly convex base when open
newRecords.caveat: The account separately reports variable serotiny; no cone-opening behavior is inferred from these structural traits.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus strobiformis seed cones as symmetric and 15–25 cm long, lance-cylindric before opening and broadly lance-cylindric when open; the apophyses are strongly cross-keeled.
newRecords.caveat: The measurements are account-level descriptive bounds, not population means.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus strobus seed cones as symmetric and 7–20 cm long, cylindric to lance-cylindric or ellipsoid-cylindric before opening, with those forms also recorded when open; the apophyses are slightly raised and resinous at the tip.
requiredSourceText: cylindric to lance-cylindric or ellipsoid-cylindric before opening
apophyses slightly raised, resinous at tip
newRecords.caveat: The account provides a broad descriptive range; this statement is not a population frequency estimate.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus torreyana seed cones as symmetric, 10–15 cm long, ovoid before opening and broadly ovoid when open; the apophyses are thick and angulately dome-shaped with five low convergent keels.
requiredSourceText: massive, heavy, symmetric, ovoid before opening
apophyses thick, angulately dome-shaped, with 5 low convergent keels
newRecords.caveat: The source's descriptive terms and dimensions are retained at account scope, without population-level frequency claims.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus virginiana seed cones as symmetric and 3–7 cm long, occasionally to 8 cm, lance-ovoid or lanceoloid before opening and ovoid when open; the scales are rigid and the apophyses slightly thickened and elongate.
requiredSourceText: symmetric, lance-ovoid or lanceoloid before opening
newRecords.caveat: The account-level dimensions do not establish the frequency of sizes in sampled populations.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus serotina seed cones as symmetric and 5–8 cm long, ovoid to lanceoloid before opening and broadly ovoid to nearly globose when open; the apophyses are low, rhombic and low cross-keeled.
requiredSourceText: often whorled, symmetric, ovoid to lanceoloid before opening
broadly ovoid to nearly globose when open
apophyses slightly thickened, low, rhombic, low cross-keeled
newRecords.caveat: The name Pinus serotina and the account's separate serotiny observations do not determine broader reproductive or ecological behavior; this claim is morphology only.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus elliottii seed cones as symmetric and 7–18 cm long, occasionally to 20 cm, lance-ovoid before opening and ovoid or ovoid-cylindric when open; the apophyses are lustrous, slightly raised and strongly cross-keeled.
requiredSourceText: single or in pairs, symmetric, lance-ovoid before opening
newRecords.caveat: The cited range is an account-level description, not a population distribution.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus sabiniana seed cones as nearly symmetric and 15–25 cm long, ovoid before opening and broadly to narrowly ovoid or ovoid-cylindric when open; the curved apophyses and umbos form upcurved claws to 2 cm.
requiredSourceText: broadly to narrowly ovoid or ovoid-cylindric when open
apophyses elongate, curved, continuous with umbos to form long, upcurved claws to 2cm
newRecords.caveat: The source describes heavy cones but provides no population-level frequency or mass estimate; only form and length are claimed.

newRecords.claim: The 2003 Flora of North America account describes Pinus clausa seed cones as symmetric, rarely slightly asymmetric, and 3–8 cm long, lanceoloid before opening and ovoid to broadly ovoid when open; the apophyses are thickened and cross-keeled.
requiredSourceText: ovoid to broadly ovoid when open
newRecords.caveat: The account separately mentions serotiny and persistence; those behaviors are not included in this morphology claim.
